deep_dive.title: Generative Modeling via Nonlinear Schrödinger Bridges and Branching Diffusions
deep_dive.abstract: We propose a new generative modeling framework grounded in forward-backward partial differential equations (PDEs). These equations arise naturally in mean-field game (MFG) theory, and are closely related to nonlinear Schrödinger systems. Our main contribution is to reinterpret this connection within the setting of generative modeling and to develop an efficient numerical methodology for its practical implementation. Specifically, we derive and characterize a nonlinear extension of the classical Schrödinger bridge problem through a coupled system of PDEs, yielding a model we call SBNL (Schrödinger Bridge NonLinear). To compute its solution, we design a simulation algorithm based on branching diffusions and the probabilistic representation of semilinear PDEs. The resulting method is embarrassingly parallel, scalable to high dimensions, and applicable to a broad class of nonlinear interaction functionals. We validate the approach through numerical experiments, including recovery of the classical Schrödinger bridge, nonlinear extensions with convex penalties (Gross-Pitaevskii) as well as potential interaction terms, and high-dimensional generative tasks such as image synthesis on the MNIST and FFHQ human face dataset. Furthermore, the same framework embeds score-based generative modeling, diffusion models, and tractable gaussian Schrödinger bridges.

deep_dive.title: Schrödinger-Bass Bridge Barycenter Models for Measure-Valued Data
deep_dive.abstract: Barycenter models, based on stochastic and deterministic optimal transport bridges between probability measures, have proven to be useful for supervised and unsupervised learning for (probability) measure-valued data. In this paper, we utilize the directional asymmetry and dual drift-diffusion control arising in the recently proposed Schrödinger-Bass Bridge (SBB) between two measures, and propose \textit{SBB-encoder}, \textit{SBB-decoder}, \textit{SBB-symmetric}, and \textit{SBB-Markovian} barycenter models. For each of these novel models, our first theoretical result establishes the existence of the SBB-barycenter under mild assumptions. Our second theoretical result characterizes the decoder SBB-barycenter of Gaussians where we show that for Gaussian input measures, the decoder formulation admits a Gaussian minimizer, reducing barycenter computation to a finite-dimensional optimization and yielding a compact algorithm. For general input measures, we derive a hybrid Wasserstein gradient particle descent scheme for all four formulations using the SBB dual representation. Finally, we utilize these algorithms for solving distributional-inverse/interpolation problems arising in the context of spatial images and single-cell RNA sequencing data, where we show that the SBB-decoder and Markovian barycenter allow us to interpolate between successive time points. Results show that our method outperforms existing barycenter models for measure interpolation and inference.

deep_dive.title: Gradient Discrete Schrodinger Bridge Matching for Peptide Generation
deep_dive.abstract: The optimal control of a discrete Schrödinger bridge is a discrete gradient, a difference of vertex potentials, but recent models such as MadSBM instead learn a free control on the edges by cross-entropy. We prove that this leaves the action uncontrolled: cross-entropy identifies the control only up to a state-dependent shift (a gauge), and the action is $\operatorname{KL}(r\|p)$ plus a gauge term the loss never constrains. We propose GDSBM, which writes the control as a difference of vertex potentials and adds the action to the loss; pinning the gauge costs no expressiveness and makes the action a property of the model, so the penalty acts on the model and not on the gauge. On peptide generation our MadSBM reimplementation has a free-gauge action of order $10^{8}$ for a gauge-fixed value of $6.5$, against $1.5$ for GDSBM, with no quality loss that three seeds can detect. The gradient form also fits guidance, which becomes the addition of a potential: guided toward a net charge of $+3$ at pH~7, GDSBM is closer than MadSBM, over three seeds, to its exact tempered target in total variation at every guidance strength (at $β=1$, $81\%$ of samples in the target window against $74\%$, for a target of $97\%$); we claim no statistical significance.

deep_dive.title: Learning Population Dynamics with Variational Doob-Wasserstein Flow
deep_dive.abstract: This paper introduces a novel simulation-free framework for learning unbalanced population dynamics on the Riemannian Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) manifold, termed Variational Doob-Wasserstein Flow (VDWF), built upon the theory of the unbalanced mean-field Schrödinger bridge (MFSB). First, by independently learning a geometry model equipped with a data-dependent metric, our model captures the intrinsic geometric structure of population dynamics. Furthermore, leveraging Doob's h-transform, the proposed method incorporates boundary information to improve flow-based trajectory inference. For unbalanced transport, a growth model is employed to learn the dynamics while constructing intermediate mass samples in the WFR space without simulation. Additionally, we analyze the convergence rate of the proposed framework using a uniform Log-Sobolev inequality (LSI). Finally, we validate the proposed approach on multiple real-world datasets, demonstrating competitive performance in learning both balanced and unbalanced population dynamics compared with state-of-the-art methods.

deep_dive.title: Image-Domain CT Metal Artifact Reduction Using an Endpoint-Conditioned Diffusion Bridge
deep_dive.abstract: Background: Metal implants cause streaking and shading artifacts in computed tomography (CT), obscuring anatomy and distorting Hounsfield-unit (HU) values. Conventional diffusion models reconstruct images from Gaussian noise rather than directly exploiting anatomical information retained in artifact-corrupted CT.   Purpose: To develop an image-domain metal artifact reduction (MAR) method connecting artifact-corrupted and metal-free CT images through an endpoint-conditioned diffusion bridge.   Methods: The proposed RDBM-MAR method uses an endpoint-conditioned diffusion bridge and initializes reconstruction from the artifact CT image. A conditional U-Net predicts an image-domain correction from intermediate bridge states. Inference uses 10 deterministic reverse steps. We used 14,000 paired CT slices from the AAPM CT-MAR Grand Challenge, including 12,045 training, 633 validation, and 1,322 held-out test slices. One clinical benchmark case was assessed qualitatively. We compared RDBM-MAR with CycleGAN, Pix2Pix, Res-SRDiff, I2I-Mamba, and I2SB using PSNR, SSIM, MAE, and LPIPS. Statistical analysis used Friedman and paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm correction.   Results: RDBM-MAR achieved the highest PSNR (43.67 +/- 4.56 dB) and SSIM (0.9856 +/- 0.0138) and the lowest MAE (14.74 +/- 8.68 HU). All four metrics differed significantly among methods (p < 0.001). RDBM-MAR outperformed all five comparators in PSNR, SSIM, and MAE (adjusted p < 0.001); Res-SRDiff achieved the lowest LPIPS. Difference maps, HU profiles, and the clinical case showed reduced artifacts with preservation of surrounding anatomy.   Conclusions: RDBM-MAR provides a direct restoration trajectory from artifact CT toward metal-free CT, achieving strong structural fidelity and HU accuracy using 10 reverse steps.

quick_skim.title: Sequential Entropic Optimal Transport for Bayesian Inverse Problems via Multilevel Monte Carlo
quick_skim.abstract: We consider the problem of Bayesian estimation associated to inverse problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). In most cases of practical interest, one must use numerical solvers to implement computational methods based on Monte Carlo methods. This inevitably leads to an adaptation of multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) methods to reduce computational efforts to achieve a pre-specified mean square error (MSE). MLMC is based on sampling coupled versions of Bayesian posteriors associated to increasingly precise numerical solves of the PDE. In this article we present a novel method to implement MLMC based upon sequential entropic optimal transport couplings learned with light Schrödinger bridges, and correct the transport with Metropolis--Hastings steps that preserve the pairing. We bound the mean square error associated to a version of our new estimation method and show, for an elliptic inverse problem, that to achieve a MSE of $\mathcal{O}(δ^2)$ ($δ>0$) one can have an optimal cost of $\mathcal{O}(δ^{-2})$. The results feature explicit bounds on the effect of the fitted transport and of the Metropolis--Hastings correction. From a numerical perspective, on elliptic, Darcy-flow and Navier-Stokes problems, the method reduces the variance of the most precise solver by a factor of five to ten and is faster than multilevel sequential Monte Carlo [arXiv:1503.07259] at tight accuracies.

quick_skim.title: Bridge change-of-measure for propagator estimation of diffusions
quick_skim.abstract: The propagator of one-dimensional diffusions has relevant applications in statistical inference and across many disciplines. Yet it is obtained in closed form only for very few simple models. Here we analyze an importance sampling strategy based on a bridge change of measure to estimate propagators: paths are generated under an auxiliary diffusion whose bridge between the two fixed boundary points is easy to generate, and the target propagator is recovered through a Radon-Nikodym derivative or likelihood ratio correction derived from Girsanov's theorem. This method overcomes the main limitations of the crude Monte Carlo estimator, which relies on binning in state space, introducing bias and becoming inefficient with rare transitions. We apply the method to a range of benchmark processes and show that the bridge-based estimator matches the accuracy of crude Monte Carlo with orders of magnitude fewer sample paths. Finally, we elaborate on discretization schemes for the Radon-Nikodym derivative and on approximations to the best-in-class change of measure, both of which increase the efficiency of the method.

quick_skim.title: Displacement Moments and Path-Terminal Separation in Brownian Interpolant Sampling
quick_skim.abstract: Brownian stochastic interpolants connect paired endpoint samples, yet their sampling error can depend on displacement moments even when neither endpoint has a first moment. For arbitrary Borel couplings, we prove early-stopped, target-to-output KL guarantees for standard Euler sampling from the true source. A fourth displacement moment gives an explicit $O(N^{-1})$ bound; a second moment suffices for fixed-law convergence as drift error vanishes. For one fixed coupling with no displacement moment above two, original bridge-path KL stays of order one, comparison-path KL is of order $1/\log N$, and terminal KL is at most $C/N^2$ on the same grid. The path decomposition identifies the information about the source discarded by Markov projection. When the original bridge is Markov, current-state Euler sampling instead has a second-moment $O((M_2+d)/N)$ bound; finite-entropy Schroedinger bridges for the probability Brownian reference are included. We also construct a current-state learner with expected output KL consistency from iid endpoint pairs. Numerical diagnostics illustrate the distinct errors. Conditional diffusion identities specify a restoration interface, while image controls find no iterative advantage over cheap probabilistic predictors. Uniform terminal rates for general second-moment couplings remain open.

quick_skim.title: The Noise Plane: A Diffusion Bridge Across Exponent and Dispersion
quick_skim.abstract: Diffusion-based denoising commonly uses Gaussian perturbations, whereas sensor noise follows diverse signal-dependent statistical laws. In this paper, we propose $p$-Bridge, a unified measurement-indexed diffusion framework for Tweedie noise. The noise exponent $p$ describes the variance--intensity relation, while accumulated measurement $ν$ controls the noise level. Together, they define a noise plane that includes Gaussian, Poisson, and Gamma models. The stochastic bridge connects measurement distributions through independent increments, giving denoising a physical interpretation as progressive measurement accumulation. Both the starting and stopping indices can be specified, allowing restoration from an observed measurement level to a prescribed higher level. Measurement superposition yields a shared reverse-mean update, paired with a deviance-based objective for learning the required conditional mean. A latent compound Poisson--Gamma construction enables sampling at intermediate exponents. A single exponent-conditioned network adapts to different Tweedie noise models without separate training for each exponent. Experiments show that exponent conditioning improves cross-exponent robustness over fixed-exponent models. Using estimated exponents, the shared network achieves robustness comparable to an oracle-selected set of five specialist models. Experiments on synthetic images, FMD fluorescence microscopy, and multi-sensor SAR images further demonstrate its effectiveness across different signal-dependent noise regimes.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: A unified measurement-indexed diffusion framework, p-Bridge, uses stochastic bridges to connect Tweedie noise distributions across exponent and dispersion, reinterpreting denoising as progressive measurement accumulation.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对传统去噪只用高斯扰动、难以匹配传感器信号相关噪声的问题，本文提出p-Bridge这一以测量为索引的统一扩散框架。方法上用噪声指数p与累积测量ν构成噪声平面，并以随机桥通过独立增量连接不同测量分布。该框架涵盖高斯、泊松与Gamma模型，使去噪获得渐进测量累积的物理解释，并可指定起止索引实现从观测水平到更高水平的恢复。
